quiz.prompt: P(A|B) =
quiz.explain: Definition of conditional probability (P(B) > 0).

quiz.prompt: A and B independent means:
quiz.explain: Knowing B tells you nothing about A. Mutually exclusive events with non-zero probability are dependent.

quiz.prompt: With a rare positive class, a high-recall classifier's precision is usually:
quiz.explain: False positives from the huge negative class can outnumber true positives.

quiz.prompt: In sequential Bayesian updating, you start with Beta(1,1) and observe 7 heads and 3 tails. What is the posterior?
quiz.explain: The Beta-Binomial conjugate update adds successes to the first parameter and failures to the second: Beta(1+7, 1+3) = Beta(8, 4). The posterior mean is 8/12 = 0.667. (Adapted from rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch Phase 01 lesson 07-bayes-theorem quiz.json, MIT licence.)

practice.brief: For Bernoulli coin flips, plot the log-likelihood over p ∈ (0,1), find the MLE numerically (grid + scipy.optimize) and analytically (k/n), and show that the binary cross-entropy of a constant predictor p is the negative mean log-likelihood.

quiz.prompt: The MLE for a Bernoulli p from k heads in n flips is:
quiz.explain: (k+1)/(n+2) is the Laplace (Bayesian) estimate, not the MLE.

quiz.prompt: We maximise log-likelihood rather than likelihood mainly because:
options: Sums are numerically stable and easier to differentiate
quiz.explain: log is monotonic so the argmax is unchanged.

quiz.prompt: Minimising cross-entropy loss for a classifier is equivalent to:

quiz.prompt: How does MAP (Maximum A Posteriori) estimation differ from MLE (Maximum Likelihood Estimation)?
options: MAP is faster to compute than MLE
MLE always produces better results than MAP
MAP incorporates a prior distribution over parameters, equivalent to adding regularization, while MLE only uses the likelihood
MAP uses a larger dataset than MLE
quiz.explain: MAP maximizes P(data|params) * P(params) while MLE maximizes P(data|params) alone. The prior P(params) acts as regularization -- a Gaussian prior equals L2 regularization, a Laplace prior equals L1. (Adapted from rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch Phase 01 lesson 07-bayes-theorem quiz.json, MIT licence.)

quiz.prompt: Model A scores 0.9234 and Model B scores 0.9237 on 1 million test samples with p-value = 0.001. What should you conclude?

quiz.prompt: Perplexity =
quiz.explain: Perplexity is the exponentiated average negative log-likelihood per token.

quiz.prompt: KL(P‖Q) is:
quiz.explain: Gibbs' inequality gives ≥ 0; KL(P‖Q) ≠ KL(Q‖P) in general.

quiz.prompt: A uniform model over 50 tokens has perplexity:
quiz.explain: exp(log 50) = 50: 'as confused as choosing among 50'.

quiz.prompt: Why is minimizing cross-entropy equivalent to minimizing KL divergence during training?
options: Because cross-entropy and KL divergence are the same formula
Because cross-entropy = entropy + KL divergence, and the entropy of the true labels is constant, so minimizing cross-entropy minimizes KL divergence
Because KL divergence is always zero during training
Because the model's entropy equals zero at convergence
quiz.explain: H(P,Q) = H(P) + D_KL(P||Q). Since the true distribution P doesn't change during training, H(P) is constant. Minimizing H(P,Q) is the same as minimizing D_KL(P||Q) -- pushing the model toward the true distribution. (Adapted from rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch Phase 01 lesson 09-information-theory quiz.json, MIT licence.)

quiz.prompt: Why can't you compare perplexity across two models that use different tokenizers?
rubric: Perplexity is per token and token units differ

capstone.title: "Is model B really better?" eval report
capstone.brief: Compare two systems (two classifiers from M07, or two prompts/models on a labelled Q&A set of ≥ 200 items). Deliver a notebook + 2-page report: metric choice, Wilson + paired-bootstrap CIs, a sample-size/power statement, slice analysis, calibration plot, judge–human kappa, and a ship/no-ship recommendation with caveats. Pass: ≥ 7/10 with no 0s.

levels: 2: computes required n for the stated MDE; addresses peeking/multiple tests
2: both, with a finding that changes or confirms the recommendation
2: kappa + disagreements analysed + judge prompt revised
2: clear decision, explicit limitations, what would change the decision
